page.name: Building the layer yourself vs using one
page.h1: Building the sending layer yourself vs using one
page.metaTitle: Build vs buy for dependable messaging
page.metaDescription: The work between “we can call an API” and “messaging is dependable”: pacing and failover on the SMS channel, normalized receipts, suppression and logs — kept off your roadmap.
page.lede: Calling a provider API takes an afternoon. Making messaging dependable is a list of unglamorous problems that only show up in production — and that list is what we maintain so your team does not have to.

sections.h: The list we keep off your roadmap
bullets: Per-number pacing, at the limit your provider actually applies to the number
Failover across accounts, plus telling an outage from a bad route (SMS channel)
Receipt normalization, so you read one status instead of every provider’s vocabulary
Suppression that catches opt-outs exactly, and does not catch them by accident
Logs that answer a support question while holding metadata rather than message bodies
A record of what was sent, per recipient, provable after the fact

sections.h: Why this is worth buying rather than building
p: None of it is hard in isolation. Each item is discovered from an incident, fixed under pressure, and then maintained as providers change their behavior. Buying the layer is how that maintenance stops being your team’s problem — and how nobody gets paged at 3am for a provider’s rate-limit change.

sections.h: Keep the parts that are yours
p: Your application still owns the decision to send, the content, and the record that matters to your business. You can route some traffic through the layer and leave the rest direct — the accounts stay yours, so the choice is reversible at any point.

faq.q: Can we use the platform for some traffic and direct for the rest?
faq.a: Yes. The platform connects to accounts you already have, so a subset of traffic can route through it while the rest continues unchanged.
Yes — sends go over HTTP with per-tenant keys, and the SMS channel is the published reference today. The API reference lists each endpoint with its request shape.

faq.q: What does the platform take off my team’s plate?
faq.a: A specific list of responsibilities — pacing and failover on the SMS channel, receipt normalization, suppression and logs — maintained as providers change their behavior. Everything else, including your own product, stays with your team.
